title: A confirm with a typed ceiling always comes back stale, and the fresh receipt marks nothing
body:
## Summary
The receipt's token binds ceilingUsd, but the sheet's receipt is read without one, so the first ⏎ after typing a ceiling is refused stale and re-shows an identical receipt with zero marks.

## Description
packages/kernel/src/records/receipt.ts:112 tokenOf hashes `ceilingUsd: i.ceilingUsd ?? null`; packages/kernel/src/records/launch.ts:55-64 planReceiptIn re-prices WITH the confirm's ceiling and launch.ts:88 refuses `fresh.token !== token`. app/(studio)/projects/_plan/receipt.tsx:75 reads the receipt `spec.read("dry")` with no ceiling, and :119 confirms with `c.value`. So a typed ceiling guarantees a stale answer; receipt.tsx:124 then shows the fresh receipt with receiptChanges(...) - and packages/ui/src/components/produce/produce.ts receiptChanges compares no ceiling, so changeCount is 0: the operator sees the same receipt, no `changed N`, and must press ⏎ again. Fixed is one of: the ceiling leaves the token (it is a stop point the confirm carries, not an input the receipt prices), or the read carries the ceiling so the token the operator holds already binds it, or receiptChanges marks `ceiling` (TotalField) so the re-show says why.

## Flow
- operator opens a receipt, types 20 in the ceiling field, presses ⏎
- useReceipt.confirm -> spec.confirm(token, 20, mode) -> launchProject: fresh token (ceiling 20) != read token (ceiling null) -> conflict stale-receipt
- sheet re-renders the fresh receipt; changes = receiptChanges(old, fresh) = 0 marks
- second ⏎ launches

## Expected impact
Every ceilinged launch costs a silent extra round-trip and reads as a dropped press; a hurried operator may press Esc thinking it failed. Could break: an MCP or CLI caller that relies on the ceiling being bound into the token.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a ceilinged confirm launches on the first ⏎, or says why not
Before: walked: tokenOf includes ceilingUsd; read omits it; 1 ceilinged confirm = 1 stale + 0 marks
After: predicted: 0 stale on an unchanged plan (or >=1 mark naming the ceiling)
Method: simulation - read across kernel launch.ts, receipt.ts and app receipt.tsx; the instrument is a next-server test over the fixture or real port (read dry -> confirm with ceilingUsd -> expect launched), not buildable inside this context's paths
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: tests/next-server case: projects port read(dry) -> confirm(token, ceilingUsd: 20) on an unchanged plan; assert kind === 'launched' (or 'stale' with changeCount > 0)

title: The ceiling crossing is spelled three times and the Receipt ignores the server's overCeiling
body:
## Summary
Whether the worst case crosses the ceiling is computed by the kernel, the fixture schedule and the UI with two different comparisons, and the Receipt never reads the server's verdict.

## Description
packages/kernel/src/records/receipt.ts:158 `exposure > i.ceilingUsd` (no epsilon); app/(studio)/projects/_port/schedule.ts:217 `top > r.ceilingUsd + 1e-9`; packages/ui/src/components/produce/produce.ts mayStopAtCeiling `top > ceiling + 1e-9`. packages/ui/src/components/produce/Receipt.tsx computes `over` locally from the typed text and never reads `receipt.overCeiling` (packages/domain/src/produce.ts:112), so the mark the screen shows and the `overCeiling` the launch event records (launch.ts:152) are two computations. Fixed: one exported predicate (domain or kernel) used by all three, and the Receipt either reads `overCeiling` when the typed ceiling equals `receipt.ceilingUsd` or a test pins that the two agree.

## Flow
- walk: kernel totals are round2'd and parseCeiling admits 2 decimals, so the epsilon difference needs a total and ceiling equal to the cent - predicted unreachable today
- the drift risk is the third spelling, not today's value

## Expected impact
Low today; removes a future disagreement between the receipt's mark and the recorded event. Could break nothing visible.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule, one implementation
Before: 3 spellings (2 comparisons), Receipt reads 0 of 1 server verdicts
After: 1 spelling, verdict pinned equal by a test
Method: simulation - kernel and app/_port are outside this context's paths
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: for receipts built by kernel receiptFor over a grid of totals x ceilings, assert receipt.overCeiling === mayStopAtCeiling(receipt, ceiling)

title: A total with unpriced lines is a floor but is drawn as a plain figure
body:
## Summary
When some lines are unpriced, the receipt's and the Estimate's cost total is a lower bound (domain says so) yet reads as a number.

## Description
packages/domain/src/produce.ts:83 `usd`: 'a lower bound whenever unpriced > 0'. packages/ui/src/components/produce/Receipt.tsx draws `cost $4.80` beside an `unpriced 1` chip, Composer.tsx Estimate draws `$4.80` beside `unpriced · seat`; the figure itself carries no floor mark. cost-metering golden path ('The unit axis is open'): 'a row carrying residual units has a cost that is a floor, not a number, and the floor propagates to every total'. Fixed: the total is written as a floor (e.g. `≥$4.80`, a shape not a sentence) wherever unpriced > 0 - receipt, Estimate, PlanSummary (app) and the Board's spendWords (lib) - from one writer in produce.ts.

## Flow
- receipt with Nano ($0.96) + Suno (credits)
- today: `cost $0.96` + `unpriced 1`
- proposed: `cost ≥$0.96` + `unpriced 1`

## Expected impact
The operator reads the priced part as the bill's ceiling rather than its floor. Could break: live specs matching exact `$` text on mixed receipts.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a partial total cannot be read as the whole bill
Before: mixed receipts drawing a floor mark: 0 of 4 surfaces
After: 4 of 4
Method: simulation - the glyph is a vocabulary choice that spans app/ and lib/ surfaces; needs a render test plus a /kit photograph (cx-capture kit-produce) to confirm it reads
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: produce.test.ts render case (mixed receipt -> /≥\$0\.96/) + cx-capture of the kit produce specimen, opened
drain_note: spans ui, app and lib, needs a /kit photo; L

title: Compose draws an empty select when no proven style, kept take or topic exists
body:
## Summary
ComposeDialog's three source selects render with zero options and an empty value when the port returns none, and nothing shows the absence.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/produce/ComposeDialog.tsx Src maps `options` straight into <option>s; with `styles: []` the select is an empty control (the existing compose test passes styles: [] and asserts nothing about it). The header says the choices are 'proven styles only, kept takes only', so an empty shelf is a real state on a fresh store. Fixed: an empty source draws the Ghost/empty shape of @gt/ui (count 0, spoken label) in place of the select, and a recipe that needs it is disarmed - per the narration law, a shape, not a sentence.

## Flow
- fresh store: no proven style
- open Compose
- style row shows an empty dropdown; picking a recipe fails server-side

## Expected impact
First-run operators see a broken-looking control. Could break: the kit specimen's layout.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an empty source reads as empty
Before: empty-source rows drawing an empty shape: 0 of 3
After: 3 of 3
Method: simulation - needs a render test and a photograph of the popover (cx-capture projects compose) to decide the shape; not taken this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/ui/src/components/produce/ComposeDialog.tsx Src
packages/ui/test/components/produce.test.ts 'compose gives the first three recipes' (styles: [])
instrument: render case with styles/takes/topics [] asserting the Ghost shape and a disarmed dependent recipe, plus cx-capture

title: Estimate and Receipt disagree on whether a banded line with usd null is unpriced
body:
## Summary
Estimate treats `usd === null` as unpriced, Receipt/PlanTable treat `usd === null && usdRange === undefined` - two predicates.

## Description
Rejected: kernel priceLine (packages/kernel/src/records/receipt.ts:33) derives usd from usdPerUnit, and every band source sets usdPerUnit (kernel options.ts usdOf, app fixtureData.ts opt midpoint, lib scoutReel REEL_USD), so the disagreeing input is unconstructible; unifying is churn.

## Flow
- grep usdRangePerUnit: every producer sets a point usdPerUnit beside the band

## Expected impact
None.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality
Before: 0 reachable inputs where the predicates differ
After: 0
Method: probe - grep of every usdRangePerUnit writer
Result: not-better
Gate: none
